grounding_notes: Reconstructed 2026-08-08 from the real 2026-07-14 fusion decision, as the regression fixture for this skill. The 23 candidates, the 9 screens, every absorption and the one dissolution are verbatim from the fusion map; the archetype per screen, the navigation edges and the menu order are this skill's own vocabulary applied to that decision, not statements the source made.

N = 9, not the 8 the fusion table proposed: the human gate split Custom Scoring out of the Search Console, on the grounds that storing a Painless script is a different job from running a query. The human gate can split a fusion, and did.

data_bindings carry only assets the source document names. The fusion map is an IA decision record, not a data model — the tenant scan behind it found roughly 30 server actions and 7 entities whose names were never written down. Where a binding is thin here, that is the source's limit being reported rather than hidden.
Index_LoadData resolves to TWO screens: its reference half is onboarding and its console half is an index operation. A candidate splitting across screens is legitimate and the contract allows it.

candidates.rationale: The landing page was a bitmap of a slide. It is where the copy-paste audience arrives and it had no code companion at all.
The only true onboarding page in the app. Stays unique because onboarding is a one-time linear task and does not belong inside a console.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §3 row 3 — holds 50 queries, not the 33 first reported
candidates.rationale: A catalogue OVER the consoles. Folding it into one console would privilege that console over the others.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §2 — code companion populated and correct
candidates.rationale: Single-query mode of one console. Near-clone of Search_Multiple, minus a labelled index field and the query-notes panel.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §1 — the app's most mature screen
candidates.rationale: Multi-query mode of the same console, and the pattern donor: it already carries the live-console-beside-code-companion arrangement the redesign propagates.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §2 — code companion present but empty
candidates.rationale: Template mode of the same console. Three screens differing by which query shape is submitted is one screen with a mode selector.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §3 row 4b — added at the gate
candidates.rationale: Stays standalone: storing a scoring script is a different job from running a query. This was the fusion flagged as least confident, and the gate split it back out.
One index operation among six. The operations differ by payload, not by screen.
One index operation among six; destructive treatment is a state of the console, not a screen.
Listing indexes is the console's own resting state — it is what you see before choosing an operation.
One index operation among six.
Index creation with mappings. The Adv_ prefix said advanced; the job is index creation.
Index settings. Same prefix, same misfiling.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §3 rows 2 and 5 — split across both
candidates.rationale: Two different jobs on one page. 'How do I bulk-load' (Kibana upload, Logstash, programmatic) is documentation and belongs in onboarding; actually loading data is an index operation and belongs in the console.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §2 — code companion populated but text wrong
candidates.rationale: One of four near-clones. The proof they are clones is in the defects: three carry Create's notes verbatim.
Copy-paste sibling of CRUD_Create; retrieval is a mode, not a destination.
Copy-paste sibling; needs the request-body region, which the console shows conditionally.
Copy-paste sibling; the only difference that matters is destructive treatment, which is a state.

candidates.source_ref: fusion-map §4 — 'a thin form over a deep engine'
candidates.rationale: The operational half of migration. The screen the redesign's biggest win sits on.
Re-indexing IS migration, and it returns an async task with no link to the screen that polls it. Fusing closes that loop.
The screen that polls the async task ReIndex returns. It is the other end of a loop that was never connected.
Stays standalone: admin CRUD over a different entity. Configuring a migration is a different job from operating one.

candidates.dissolved_into: An inline escape affordance beside every raw-DSL textarea, on whichever console holds one.
candidates.rationale: It was never a destination. Nobody navigates somewhere to escape a string — they need it where they are already typing.

screens.name: Start
screens.purpose: Route a developer to the screen that demonstrates the API they came for.
screens.behavior: Presents the app's capabilities as native cards, each API name deep-linking to the console that demonstrates it. Replaces a bitmap of a slide with the app's actual router.
key_interactions: Select a capability card to jump to the console that demonstrates it
Read a one-line description of each capability without leaving the page

screens.name: Setup
screens.purpose: Take a first-time user from an empty tenant to a working, populated index.
screens.behavior: Walks the one-time setup as visible steps on one page — connection, then the three bulk-load routes (Kibana upload, Logstash, programmatic) absorbed from the reference half of the old load-data screen. Steps are visible, not hidden behind Next.
key_interactions: Work down the setup steps in order, each independently checkable
Copy a bulk-load snippet for the chosen route
Continue into the Index Console once an index exists

screens.name: Query Library
screens.purpose: Browse the stored query catalogue and open any of them in the right console.
screens.behavior: A filterable card grid over the stored queries, one card per query with its snippet visible, deep-linking into the console that runs it. Activates the tag taxonomy the old screen carried but never used.
key_interactions: Filter the grid by tag
Read a query's snippet from its card without opening it
Open a query in the Search Console pre-loaded

data_bindings.name: GetRecordsByQuery
data_bindings.usage: Reads the stored query catalogue for the grid.
data_bindings.behavior_notes: Named in the source only as the action wrongly displayed on Adv_FunctionScore's code panel; its result shape must be re-verified against the tenant before a blueprint binds to it.

screens.name: Search Console
screens.purpose: Run any search shape against an index and show the request beside the result.
screens.behavior: One console with a Single / Multi / Template mode selector, replacing three near-identical screens. Every mode shows the live request beside the OUTSYSTEMS CODE companion panel — the pattern the app already invented on Search_Multiple and denied to everything else — and returns a tabbed response.
key_interactions: Choose Single, Multi or Template mode
Pick a target index
Submit the query and read the tabbed response
Copy the accompanying action snippet from the code companion
Escape a raw DSL string inline, beside the textarea

data_bindings.name: GetRecordsByQuery
data_bindings.usage: Executes the composed query for all three modes.
data_bindings.behavior_notes: Signature must be re-verified per mode: the source records that the three old screens differed by query shape, and it does not record whether one action covered all three.

screens.name: Custom Scoring
screens.purpose: Store and manage Painless scoring scripts, and show which queries use each.
screens.behavior: Lists the stored scripts and edits one at a time. Closes a loop the old screen left open by showing, per script, which queries consume it and linking back into the Search Console.
key_interactions: Select a stored script from the list to edit it
Save a script and see it appear in the list
See which queries use the selected script
Follow a usage link back into the Search Console

data_bindings.name: StoreFunctionScoreScript
data_bindings.behavior_notes: This is the action the old screen was actually for. Its code panel advertised GetRecordsByQuery instead — the wrong action name shipped on the screen, which is why the binding is stated explicitly here.

screens.name: Index Console
screens.purpose: Perform every index-level operation from one place.
screens.behavior: Lists existing indexes as its resting state, then performs a chosen operation against one: create, create-with-mappings, delete, set alias, adjust real-time settings, or load data. Six former screens become an operation selector because they differ by payload, not by task.
key_interactions: See the current indexes on arrival, before choosing anything
Choose an index operation
Fill the operation's payload and submit it
Confirm before a destructive operation runs
Escape a raw DSL string inline, beside the textarea

screens.name: Document Console
screens.purpose: Create, retrieve, update and delete a single document against an index.
screens.behavior: One console with a CRUD mode selector, replacing four screens that were one screen copy-pasted four times. The request-body region appears only for Create and Update; Delete carries destructive treatment.
key_interactions: Choose Create, Retrieve, Update or Delete
Supply the document id and, for Create/Update only, the request body
Submit and read the response
Confirm before a delete runs

screens.name: Migration Console
screens.purpose: Tell an operator whether a migration run is alive, progressing, or stuck — and act on it.
screens.behavior: Surfaces the migration engine the old screen hid: run status as a badge rather than raw text, progress against expected-vs-indexed, the per-record failure log, retry and attempt tracking, and the heartbeat/stale-bucket signal that answers 'is the worker dead?'. Absorbs re-index (which starts a run) and task management (which polls it), closing a loop that had no link between its ends.
key_interactions: Read run status and progress at a glance
Start a re-index run and land on the run it created
Open the per-record failure log for a run
Retry a failed record
See the worker heartbeat and whether a bucket has gone stale
Open the profile a run was configured from

data_bindings.name: ESMigrationFailure
data_bindings.usage: Per-record failure log for the selected run.
data_bindings.behavior_notes: A whole entity with zero UI in the old app. It is a per-RECORD log, so its volume scales with the migration, not with the run count — the screen needs paging from the start.

screens.name: Migration Profiles
screens.purpose: Manage the reusable configurations migration runs are started from.
screens.behavior: Admin CRUD over migration profiles. Configuration only — starting and watching a run is the Migration Console's job, and keeping the two apart is why this screen was not fused into it.
key_interactions: Browse existing profiles in a table
Create or edit a profile
Delete a profile, with confirmation
Start a run from a profile and follow it into the Migration Console

navigation.trigger: open the scoring script a query uses
follow a usage link back to the query
work with documents in the selected index
open the profile a run was configured from
start a run from this profile
